title: Book a flight: two rules, one gateway
lede: Muse calls the Agent Gateway to book a flight. The gateway looks up the fare and your agent limit, then asks PingOne Authorize, which reads the member tier from the PingOne user (airlineMemberTier). Two rules can stop it: yours (no tickets bought by an AI agent over your limit) and the airline's (only premium members over $750). Mock is a local stand-in for Authorize; Real needs your tenant.

lanes.label: Muse, Agent Gateway, PingOne Authorize and the airline server

nodes.label: 1. Muse (the app)
sub: Personal Agent acts for Sam, or Sam books directly

nodes.label: 2. Agent Gateway
sub: The only way to the airline tool
Looks up the facts, asks Authorize

nodes.label: 3. Fare + agent limit
sub: Fare by flight, agent spend limit

nodes.label: 4. PingOne Authorize
sub: Your rule: no tickets bought by an AI agent over your limit ($500)
Airline rule: only premium members can book over $750
Reads the tier from the PingOne user (airlineMemberTier)

steps.title: tools/call
steps.what: Muse sends tools/call for book_airline_flight with a flight number and an amount. It never sends a tier, a limit or a token in the arguments.
steps.why: The model never writes arguments, and a caller's price is a claim, not a fact.

steps.title: Facts lookup
steps.what: The gateway looks up the fare for that flight and the member's agent spend limit from its own read-only data. The amount Muse sent is overwritten. It does not look up the member tier.
steps.why: A caller cannot lower the price that is judged or raise its own limit.

steps.title: Authorize request
steps.what: The gateway asks PingOne Authorize with the attributes: ToolName, Amount, DecisionContext, ActClientId (empty for a direct caller), AgentSpendLimit, and the user's subject. It does not send a tier.
steps.why: Both rules decide from facts the gateway or the PingOne user holds, not from what the caller says.

steps.title: Decision
steps.what: Authorize applies both rules. Your rule only applies when an agent is acting and fare is over your limit. Authorize reads the member tier itself, from the PingOne user attribute airlineMemberTier (Premier Gold is premium; any other value or none is not). The airline rule applies to everyone: over $750 needs a premium tier. Exactly $500 and exactly $750 pass. Every rule that denied is named.
steps.why: Two owners, two rules, one decision. Both are reported when both fail.

steps.title: Tool runs only on PERMIT
steps.what: On PERMIT the gateway forwards the call to the airline MCP server. On DENY it answers HTTP 403 and the tool never runs. A permit still meets the consent gate in Real (HTTP 428).
steps.why: A stopped booking is stopped before the airline server sees it.

steps.title: Result to Muse
steps.what: The result comes back to Muse. A booking adds a ledger row; a deny leaves the ledger empty and Muse shows which rule applied.
steps.why: The proof that nothing was booked is the empty ledger.
